keyVerseText: Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us;
rootMeaning: The word τηλικοῦτος (tēlikoûtos) is a compound formed from the Greek definite article ὁ (ho, meaning 'the' or 'this') combined with ἡλίκος (hēlikos) meaning 'of such an age or size' and οὗτος (houtos) meaning 'this.' Literally, it conveys the sense of 'of this magnitude' or 'of such a degree.' This root sense emphasizes not merely a qualitative descriptor but a measure of extent or size, whether in age, degree, or magnitude, going beyond a simple English gloss like 'so great' to highlight a tangible comparison or scale.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, τηλικοῦτος appears four times and is primarily translated as 'so great' three times and once as 'so mighty.' This shows a consistent usage emphasizing vastness or strength, whether referring to persons or things. The term can describe age, youth, or extent, but in the biblical context given, it mainly highlights the enormity or power of something, underscoring its figurative magnitude rather than a literal physical size.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, τηλικοῦτος enriches our understanding of God's power and providence by expressing the overwhelming greatness or might involved in His acts. When Scripture uses this term, it draws attention to the vastness of God's deliverance, protection, or judgment, inviting believers to trust in His incomparable strength. Recognizing this word's emphasis on magnitude reminds Christians of the surpassing greatness of divine intervention, encouraging faith in God's ability to rescue and sustain us beyond human capacity. It also humbles us by contrasting God's mighty acts against our limited human experience.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Corinthians 1:10, the phrase 'so great a death' employs τηλικοῦτος to emphasize the overwhelming severity and danger from which God delivered Paul and his companions. This word deepens the verse by highlighting the vastness of the threat and, consequently, the greatness of God's saving power. It assures believers that the same mighty deliverance they experienced in the past will continue, fostering confident trust in God's ongoing protection and faithfulness.
